trip.title: Oʻahu, 5 nights · Jan 3–9
trip.subtitle: Leave the Toronto snow behind and fly into the warm wind of the middle of the Pacific. The first full day belongs to Pearl Harbor, standing quietly for a while in the white memorial above the USS Arizona. Then one day in a car around the island: a botanical garden walled by green cliffs, the ranch valleys from the Jurassic films, a plate of garlic shrimp on the North Shore with turtles dozing on the sand, and after dark at Ko Olina, a sky full of stars. Later, snorkel among the coral at Hanauma Bay, look out to sea from below Diamond Head, and sail out after the sunset. On the last night, finish dinner to Hawaiian steel guitar and the afterglow, then slip away from the island in the dark.

days.title: Sun · Nonstop to Honolulu, late check-in

schedule.title: Arrive at Pearson
schedule.text: Nonstop flights to the US clear US preclearance in Toronto, so arrive 2.5–3 hours before departure. Even if you don't need a visa, double-check passport validity.

schedule.title: AC589 departs
schedule.text: ~10 hours nonstop. Try to sleep on Hawaii time on the plane; Hawaii is 5 hours behind Toronto.

schedule.title: Land in Honolulu
schedule.text: Domestic arrival, no immigration again. After baggage claim, taxi or Uber to the hotel, ~25–30 min, ~USD40–50.

schedule.title: Hotel check-in
schedule.text: Let the hotel know you'll arrive late so the room isn't released.

days.title: Mon · Full day at Pearl Harbor's four sites; sunset sail in the early evening if the weather's good

schedule.title: Jet-lagged early start, breakfast
schedule.text: You'll wake up early the first few days, perfect for Pearl Harbor. No driving.

schedule.title: Uber to Pearl Harbor
schedule.text: ~25 min. No bags allowed, only small clear bags or phone wallets; paid bag storage available.

schedule.title: USS Arizona Memorial
schedule.text: Reservations are free, with only a small booking fee. Released on Recreation.gov; book the earliest slot. Includes a film and boat ride, ~75 min.

schedule.title: Submarine Museum / USS Bowfin
schedule.text: Right next to the visitor center; included in the Passport.

schedule.title: Shuttle to Ford Island · USS Missouri
schedule.text: The deck where Japan signed the surrender; grab a simple lunch on the island afterwards.

schedule.title: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum
schedule.text: Two hangars, ~1.5 hours. Shuttle back to the visitor center afterwards.

schedule.title: Back to Waikīkī
schedule.text: After the aviation museum, shuttle back to the visitor center, then Uber ~25 min, arriving around 16:00.

schedule.title: Backup: Waikīkī sunset sail
schedule.text: The sunset sail can be today or Jan 7: check the weather and sea conditions before the trip and pick whichever day is calmer with fewer clouds. If today, be at the beach boarding spot at 16:30, sailing 17:00–19:00; you'll still be adjusting to the time change, so if you're tired save it for Jan 7. No sail? Stroll Kūhiō Beach and watch the sunset (~18:05 in January).

schedule.title: Dinner: Duke's Waikiki
schedule.text: Oceanfront; fish and Hula Pie. Reserve ahead; if you sail today, book 19:15.

days.title: Tue · The only driving day: botanical garden, Jurassic ranch tour, shrimp and turtles, Dole Plantation, then stargazing at Ko Olina

schedule.title: Pick up the car in Waikīkī
schedule.text: Bring your G licence and credit card; inspect the car and take photos. Clockwise loop today: the northeast valleys first, then back along the North Shore.

schedule.title: Hoʻomaluhia Botanical Garden
schedule.text: Opens at 9:00. Drive in, park by the lake for mountain photos, and walk a short stretch. Skipping Byodo-In this time, so you can linger here.

schedule.title: Kualoa Ranch Jurassic Adventure
schedule.text: Check in at the ranch around 10:40. Ride an off-road vehicle into the Kualoa, Hakipuʻu and Kaʻaʻawa valleys to see filming spots from Jurassic Park, Jurassic World and more. Bumpy ride, only short walks. Book your slot ahead.

schedule.title: Giovanni's garlic shrimp
schedule.text: Lunch. If the line is too long, try Romy's or Fumi's next door. Then head west on Kamehameha Hwy; just glance at Shark's Cove and Waimea Bay from the car: North Shore surf is big on winter afternoons, so no dedicated stops.

schedule.title: Turtle watching at Laniakea
schedule.text: Turtles often haul out to bask in the afternoon; watch from shore for 15 min and keep your distance. Roadside parking is tight; if there's no spot, go straight to Dole.

schedule.title: Dole Plantation: train + maze
schedule.text: Ride the Pineapple Express train first (~20 min, roughly every 10 min; the official site suggests 1 hour including the pineapple-cutting demo), then the Pineapple Garden Maze (40 min on average), and finish with Dole Whip. Park hours 9:30–17:30; the last train and last maze entry aren't listed online, so call 808-621-8408 before you go. If the last train is early, do the maze first.

schedule.title: Waikele Premium Outlets
schedule.text: ~20 min from Dole via H-2. Shop for ~50 min only; if you run late at Dole, skip it and go straight to Ko Olina for dinner.

schedule.title: Ko Olina dinner
schedule.text: ~18 min drive from the outlets (~35 min straight from Dole). Eat inside the Ko Olina resort area, e.g. Monkeypod Kitchen; reservations recommended.

schedule.title: Stargazing · Stars Above Hawaii
schedule.text: An astronomy guide with a computerized telescope talks about Hawaiian star navigation, ~1 hour, and photos are sent to your phone. Jan 7 is the new moon, so these are the darkest nights. Start time depends on the slot you book; you'll get a text that afternoon about weather and the viewing spot. Weather cancellations get a full refund or rebooking.

schedule.title: Drive back to Waikīkī
schedule.text: ~45 min, back at the hotel around 21:45. Take it easy on the roads at night; it's a long day. Park at the hotel overnight (~USD45) and return the car tomorrow morning.

days.title: Wed · Return the car, downtown by trolley

schedule.title: Fill up and return the car
schedule.text: Return by the time on your booking; being late may cost an extra day.

schedule.title: Start the Waikiki Trolley 4-day pass
schedule.text: 4-day all-line pass ~USD150 for two, hop on/hop off, good for Jan 6–8. Take the Red Line (downtown history line) to the palace.

schedule.title: ʻIolani Palace
schedule.text: The only royal palace in the US; open Tue–Sat, tickets online only.

schedule.title: King Kamehameha Statue, Chinatown
schedule.text: The statue is right across from the palace; take the Red Line or walk to Chinatown.

schedule.title: Seafood lunch at Nico's Pier 38
schedule.text: Not on a trolley line; Uber ~10 min. Poke bowls and fried fish.

schedule.title: Ala Moana Center
schedule.text: Pink Line (Ala Moana shopping line) both ways.

schedule.title: Dinner in Waikīkī
schedule.text: Hanauma Bay tomorrow morning, so turn in early.

days.title: Thu · Guided snorkel tour, Diamond Head lookout, sunset sail in the early evening

schedule.title: Roberts Hawaii Hanauma Bay transfer tour
schedule.text: Includes entry and round-trip transport from Waikīkī, ~USD65/person; snorkel gear not included, rent it at the bay. Bookable up to one month ahead.

schedule.title: Snorkeling
schedule.text: Watch the preserve video first, then snorkel in the inner bay. Decide on swimming and fins based on your own fitness, lifeguard guidance and the day's conditions. If it's closed or conditions are bad, it's also open Jan 8, so you can switch.

schedule.title: Back to the hotel to rest, lunch
schedule.text: The tour bus drops you back in Waikīkī.

schedule.title: Green Line to the Diamond Head lookout
schedule.text: The Green Line (Diamond Head Line) has a photo stop at Kahala Lookout; step off and you'll see Diamond Head and the ocean, no hiking. A loop takes ~70 min, and the last afternoon run heads back from the Diamond Head area around 15:10–15:40, so don't set out too late. Not going into the crater: that needs a separate state park reservation, and without the summit there isn't much to see.

schedule.title: Meet at the beach boarding spot
schedule.text: Usually arrive 20–30 min early. Wear shoes that are easy to board in and bring a light jacket; it's breezy on the water in the evening.

schedule.title: Waikīkī sunset sail (or move to Jan 4)
schedule.text: E.g. Moana Sailing's 2-hour sail (~USD81/person, one drink included); Manu Kai's 1.5-hour happy hour ~USD56/person. January sunset is ~18:05, and heading back after dark you'll see Waikīkī and Diamond Head lit up. Operators may cancel in rough seas. The sail can also go on the evening of Jan 4: check the forecast before the trip and pick the calmer, less cloudy day; if you already sailed on Jan 4, just watch the sunset from the beach and eat early.

schedule.title: Dinner: Waikīkī seafood
schedule.text: Eat nearby after the sail; if you missed Duke's on Jan 4, go there.

days.title: Fri · Slow day, sunset dinner, midnight departure

schedule.title: Hanauma Bay backup
schedule.text: Only if Jan 7 gets canceled; open Fridays.

schedule.title: Check out, store bags
schedule.text: Check out in the morning, leave bags at the front desk and pick them up in the evening. To shower before the airport, ask if you can use the gym or pool showers. If you went with the Expedia flight + hotel bundle, the room is booked through Jan 9, so you can use it until you leave for the airport.

schedule.title: Optional: Blue Line along the southeast coast
schedule.text: The Blue Line (Ocean View Line) runs along the coast to Hālona Blowhole (photo stop) and Sea Life Park, ~1h 50m per loop, every ~40 min from 8:30. If you'd rather not, relax on the beach or go shopping.

schedule.title: House Without A Key sunset dinner
schedule.text: Sunset and hula show; reservations recommended.

schedule.title: Head to the airport
schedule.text: ~25–30 min. The return is the Air Canada nonstop at 00:10 on Jan 9; arrive 2.5–3 hours early. If you booked the bundle, follow its transfer arrangements.

schedule.title: Air Canada nonstop departs
schedule.text: Red-eye, ~8h 41m; try to sleep on the plane.

schedule.title: Arrive in Toronto
schedule.text: Toronto time. Clear Canadian customs on the way back from the US.

items: 🚋 Green Line to Diamond Head lookout

items.title: Check your Canadian passport is valid for the whole trip
items.note: Canadians don't need a visa or ESTA for the US, but you must fly on a passport. If validity is short, airlines may apply a “6 months after leaving the US” rule, so to be safe, renew first.

items.title: Check Chinese passport validity: ideally 6+ months left after leaving the US
items.lead: Check now; renewing in Canada takes weeks
items.note: The US generally requires passports to be valid for 6 months beyond departure; countries on CBP's “Six-Month Club” list are exempt (latest version 2025-12-18). Check that list to see whether China is on it. If under 6 months, renew ASAP through the Chinese consulate in Canada.

items.title: Check the US B1/B2 visa is still valid on entry Jan 3
items.note: If the visa is in the old passport, bring both the old and new passports. Canadian PR status doesn't replace a US visa.

items.title: Complete EVUS enrollment (or confirm it's still valid)
items.lead: 2 weeks ahead recommended; at least 72 hours before departure
items.note: Chinese passport holders with a 10-year B1/B2 visa must enroll in EVUS or they'll be denied boarding. Fee USD30.75 (from Jan 2026, may rise slightly), valid 2 years; re-enroll after getting a new passport or visa. Only use the official site evus.gov; watch out for fee-charging agent sites.

items.title: Check the Canadian PR card is still valid when returning Jan 9
items.lead: Check now; PR card renewals take months
items.note: Flying back to Canada requires a valid PR card or PR travel document (PRTD); airlines don't accept an electronic COPR. If the PR card expires before Jan 9, it can only be renewed from inside Canada, and a PRTD must be applied for from abroad and takes time, so assess the trip first.

items.title: Buy travel medical insurance
items.note: Ontario's OHIP covers very little in the US, and US healthcare is expensive. If relying on credit-card insurance, confirm days covered, limits, and whether you must pay for the flights with that card.

items.title: Fill out the Hawaii plants & animals declaration form
items.note: All travelers to Hawaii must declare plants and animals they bring. You may get a paper form on board or use the official digital Akamai Arrival, depending on the flight; one per family is enough.

items.title: Book flights: {option}
items.note: AC nonstop with carry-on: Trip.com at CA$2,062 for two is cheapest but allows no changes (free cancellation within 24 hours); Air Canada's site Standard CA$2,132 allows paid changes. Basic fares don't allow a carry-on bag; don't buy them.

items.title: Book 5 hotel nights: {option} (Jan 3–8), and note the free-cancellation deadline
items.note: Lowest per hotel (5 nights incl. tax): Hotel Renew CA$1,223 (Vio), Hyatt Place CA$1,730 (Expedia, breakfast incl.), Kaimana CA$1,763 (Vio), ʻAlohilani CA$2,067 (Expedia), Sheraton CA$3,056 (Trip.com, no room change). Check the free-cancellation deadline before booking.

items.title: Reserve the earliest USS Arizona Memorial slot on Jan 4
items.lead: Released 8 weeks ahead, daily at 15:00 Hawaii time (20:00 Toronto)
items.note: Free, $1 fee per ticket, no changes or refunds. If you miss out, more tickets are released at 15:00 the day before for the next 24 hours, but on Jan 3 we'll still be on the plane, so best to book now.

items.title: Book Kualoa Ranch Jurassic Adventure (Jan 5, around 11:00)
items.note: Popular slots sell out. Book around 11:00: too early and there's no time for the botanical garden, too late and there's not enough time for Dole.

items.title: Book the one-day car rental for Jan 5: {option}
items.note: Get the full price for a 23-year-old with a Canadian G licence, incl. the under-25 surcharge, insurance and Waikīkī pickup/return. Confirm a 23-year-old can rent this model.

items.note: Includes entry and round-trip Waikīkī transport, ~USD65/person; snorkel gear not included.

items.title: Ask the hotel about storing bags on Jan 8 and using a shower
items.note: The return is a red-eye at 00:10 on Jan 9; leave bags at the front desk after checking out during the day, and ask whether the gym or pool showers are available to freshen up before the airport.

items.title: Call Dole Plantation about the last train and last maze entry on Jan 5
items.note: The official site only lists park hours 9:30–17:30. Phone 808-621-8408; if the last train is before 16:30, do the maze first, then the train.

items.title: Book Ko Olina stargazing for Jan 5; confirm that night's slots and start time
items.lead: 3–4 weeks ahead; free cancellation up to 24 hours before
items.note: The booking page doesn't say which nights it runs or when it starts (other sites have listed 20:00/21:00/22:00); confirm there's a Tuesday slot when booking, ideally 20:00. Weather cancellations get a full refund or rebooking.

items.title: Book a Waikīkī sunset sail: Jan 4 or Jan 7 (weather), departing around 17:00
items.lead: Book Jan 7 to hold a spot, then decide before the trip whether to move to Jan 4 based on the forecast
items.note: Moana Sailing 2 hours ~USD81/person; Manu Kai 1.5 hours ~USD56/person. Check change and cancellation rules before booking (many operators don't refund within 24 hours of departure), and confirm the boarding spot.

items.title: Book Ko Olina dinner for Jan 5 (19:00)
Check weather and sea conditions for the evenings of Jan 4 and Jan 7 and the night of Jan 5 to pick the sailing day
items.note: Sail on whichever of Jan 4 or Jan 7 is calmer with fewer clouds; the evening of Jan 6 works as a backup. If it's cloudy, the stargazing operator will text about rescheduling.

cash.summary: Hawaii uses US dollars, so no other local currency needed. Hotels, tours, restaurants, Uber and the trolley all take cards; cash is mainly for tips and cash-only stalls, plus a bit for emergencies. Restaurant tips are usually 18–20%, added to the card bill, no cash needed.

currencies.label: US dollars
currencies.how: Exchange CAD at a Canadian bank or currency exchange before you go. Get small bills: $1×10, $5×6, $10×4, $20×6. ATMs in Hawaii charge fees, so exchange before you leave if you can.

items.label: Guide, driver and crew tips
items.note: Ranch tour, Hanauma Bay transfer, sunset sail, stargazing guide, ~US$5–10 each

items.label: Cash-only stalls
items.note: North Shore shrimp trucks, shave ice, malasadas, farmers' markets, etc.; some don't take cards

items.label: Emergency cash
items.note: For when cards don't work; bring it home if unused

tips: Use a credit card with no foreign transaction fee; if the terminal asks whether to pay in CAD or USD, choose USD.
Most tips are added to the card bill; cash is only for in-person tips like housekeeping and guides.
